blocks.sub: What it is, what it stores, and every surface a reader can touch.

blocks.text: The cron substrate is a session-scoped, in-memory job scheduler exposed to every citizen through three calls: CronCreate, CronList, CronDelete. It stores no state on disk and vanishes when the session ends.

items.name: jobs (in-memory)
items.note: job id, cron expression, prompt, recurring flag, created-at

items.name: no persistent table
items.note: nothing survives a session restart — this is the root cause behind most findings in the companion report

boxes.name: job record
boxes.desc: One entry per CronCreate call, held in the session's in-memory table.

tables.name: id
tables.note: opaque job id, returned to caller

tables.name: recurring
tables.note: bool — false auto-deletes after first fire

blocks.title: What owns what
blocks.mermaid:
graph LR
  caller[caller] -->|CronCreate| table[(in-memory job table)]
  table -->|CronList| caller
  caller -->|CronDelete| table
  table -.->|7 days, no caller action| gone[[silently deleted]]
blocks.caption: The dashed edge is the one path with no caller in the loop — this is the shape a reader needs before they trust the table above.

steps.head: CronDelete
steps.sub: cancel before the job fires or expires

cells.text: 7 days, then final fire + silent delete
up to 10% of period, max 15 min
